business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Bulk Export of Organic Dried Lycium and Herbal Botanicals

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; relevant LLC provisions under Articles 1, 6-14, 25-27, and 33
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registration Department, One-Stop Shop
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association (AOA) together with GAFI Incorporation Application and Ministry of Justice statistical form
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an LLC under the Companies Law; the founders determine capital in the AOA, and the subscribed capital must be deposited in a provisional bank account before formal registration
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders hereby resolve that the Limited Liability Company be formed under the name stated in the Articles of Association in accordance with the Companies Law 159/1981 and Investment Law 72/2017. All shareholders subscribe to the issued capital, and receipt of capital contributions is acknowledged. The registered office is established at the address specified in the AOA. The following officers are appointed: Managing Director, Chief Financial Officer, and Company Secretary, each vested with statutory authority to execute filings, open bank accounts, and procure licenses. The board is further authorized to take all ancillary steps for registration, governance, and continuing compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / GAFI Investor Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Arabic and English company names to GAFI's electronic name-screening tool. Pay the name reservation fee and obtain the preliminary approval certificate. Retain the approved name certificate for the subsequent incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all shareholders and managers
Power of attorney for the submitting agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing trademark or registered entity, submit up to three alternative names within five working days and request written rejection grounds from GAFI for appeal or amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Association and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Regional Notary Public Office and a licensed Egyptian bank with corporate account facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the AOA in Arabic, verify all shareholder details, and sign the AOA before the Notary Public. Open a temporary capital deposit account at a bank approved by GAFI, deposit the subscribed capital, and obtain a certificate evidencing payment. No business commencement is allowed before the deposit certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Notarized AOA signed by all shareholders
Passport and national ID copies of shareholders and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires amendment to the AOA, convene a shareholders' meeting to ratify the revision, renotarize the AOA, and have the bank amend the deposit instruction accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing and Corporate Registration with GAFI
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop - Companies Registration Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized AOA, capital deposit certificate, and completed GAFI incorporation application through the One-Stop Shop. Verify the commercial registration data, pay the prescribed filing fees, and receive the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and Commercial Register excerpt.
required_dossiers: Lease contract for the registered office (min 1 year validity)
Passport and national ID copies of all signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query or deficiency notice, file a curative response within 15 days by amending the application, supplying missing documents, or correcting the AOA. If rejected, appeal to GAFI's legal affairs department within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Import/Export Code Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority and GAFI Foreign Trade Interface
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the incorporation certificate, apply electronically for the Tax Card (Karteh Dharibiya), VAT registration, payroll tax registration, and the Automatic Import/Export Register code. Register the company's customs profile for future cross-border consignments of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Commercial Register excerpt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is queried due to address proof or business classification, provide updated lease documentation or adjust the ISIC activity code through GAFI by submitting a formal amendment request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Insurance Registration and Corporate Governance Stamping
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) and the Administrative Labor Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the employer registration with NOSI, submit the payroll structure and employment contracts for legal stamping, and register all directors and staff for social insurance. Maintain statutory corporate minute books documenting the first board resolution and officer appointments.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Tax Card
Passport and ID copies of all employees and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI identifies discrepancies in salary declarations or missing dependent data, submit corrected schedules and pay the assessed adjustments within 14 days to avoid late penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) - Licensing and Compliance Department under the Ministry of Trade and Industry
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operating License (Rokhas Tashghil) for Food and Botanical Product Processing and Wholesale Storage

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Environmental Impact Assessment Report required for herbal and botanical processing facilities; discharge and waste handling plans must be approved before operation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law 4/1994 and Law 9/2009; industrial wastewater discharge must meet Decree 44/2000 limits for BOD, COD, and total suspended solids; particulate and VOC emissions limited to allowable levels under Environment Protection Regulations; hazardous waste handling must comply with Waste Management Regulation No. 874 of 2021

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Civil Defense Authority, structural load inspection for storage racking areas, and occupational safety clearance from the Ministry of Manpower evidencing compliant work environment and worker protection measures

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance, Cairo; official gate: https://www.eta.gov.eg; mandatory e-invoicing and e-receipt platform: https://invoice.eta.gov.eg; electronic customs clearance portal (NAFIZA): https://www.nafiza.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A wholly foreign-owned Egyptian LLC registers in the ETA Unified Taxpayer Registry to obtain a single Unified Tax Registration Number (TIN/VAT ID) and the statutory tax card. Procedure: (1) incorporate under Companies Law No. 159/1981 (as amended by Law No. 4/2018) through the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) one-stop shop; (2) obtain commercial registration and the activity license for ISIC 4631 (wholesale of dried botanicals and herbal products); (3) file ETA Form No. 1 (tax registration) attaching the memorandum and articles of association, GAFI certificate, commercial registry certificate, passport copies of shareholders and directors, and a board resolution appointing a resident statutory tax agent and auditor; (4) submit the VAT registration declaration (mandatory where annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 500,000, or immediately where export zero-rating input recovery is intended); (5) complete e-invoicing onboarding (ERP-to-ETA API integration) within 30 days of VAT registration; (6) open an Egyptian corporate bank account for foreign-currency export collections. ETA issues the tax card within 5-15 business days and the VAT certificate concurrently; engaging a licensed Egyptian tax accountant or fiscal representative is mandatory for filings and VAT refund claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: an Egyptian LLC is a resident juridical person (residency based on incorporation under Egyptian law) taxed under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, as amended and consolidated by Unified Tax Law No. 193 of 2024 for tax years beginning on or after 1 January 2025, at the standard CIT headline rate of 22.5%. Territorial scope: resident LLCs are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident shareholders and foreign counterparties are taxed only on Egypt-source income (10% dividend withholding tax on profit distributions, reduced to 5% for listed shares). No pass-through, transparent, or check-the-box classification exists; LLC profits are always taxed at entity level before distribution.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections are available in Egypt. Available statutory elections: (a) consolidated group CIT filing where the parent holds 95% or more of resident subsidiaries (Article 46 of Law 91/2005); (b) SME simplified presumptive tax regime under Law No. 152 of 2020 for entities with annual turnover up to EGP 20 million (elective 0.5%-2.5% of gross revenue instead of accounting-profit CIT); (c) special economic-zone status election for SCZONE or Qualified Industrial Zones allowing customs and VAT suspension on production inputs destined for export; (d) 5-year tax-loss carry-forward offset election; (e) advance pricing agreement (APA) filing with ETA for export-related inter-company pricing; (f) free-zone tax exemption election subject to revenue-yield conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended by Law No. 3 of 2023 and consolidated under Unified Tax Law No. 193 of 2024
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual value of taxable supplies triggers mandatory VAT registration; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold. An exporter of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals remains VAT-registered even with exclusively zero-rated export turnover in order to claim input VAT refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory ETA e-invoicing applies to all business taxpayers (phased rollout completed in 2023). B2B invoices must be generated in the ETA XML/JSON schema, digitally signed with an ETA-issued certificate, and submitted in real time through the ERP-to-ETA REST/API integration; each invoice is automatically validated, cleared, and stamped with an ETA billing code and QR code before delivery to the buyer. Non-submission, late submission, schema rejection, or data mismatch triggers automated tax-control risk flags and fines of EGP 10,000-50,000 per document. B2C e-receipt digital validation has applied since 2022. Export e-invoices must cross-reference the NAFIZA customs export declaration number in the mandated data fields to sustain 0% rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to supplies of goods exported by a VAT-registered exporter where: (i) the goods physically depart Egypt under a valid electronic customs export declaration filed in NAFIZA within the export period fixed by Customs Law No. 207 of 2020; (ii) carrier documents (bill of lading or airway bill) evidence exit from Egyptian customs territory; (iii) the buyer is a non-resident and consideration is received in convertible foreign currency through an Egyptian bank; and (iv) the VAT e-invoice is issued with the correct export type and customs declaration reference. Input VAT on raw materials, packaging, warehousing, inland freight, and inspection services attributable to export sales is creditable and refundable in cash; ancillary services (handling, commission, cold treatment) directly linked to and consumed with the exported dried botanicals equally qualify at 0% when supplied to the non-resident buyer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (NAFIZA release receipt with stamped AC number)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export from Egypt to the foreign port of discharge
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) / bank FX credit confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds in convertible currency
Final commercial invoice identical in content to the cleared ETA e-invoice (billing code quoted)
Signed export sales contract / purchase order with incoterms and non-resident buyer identification
Phytosanitary certificate, certificate of origin, and packing list for the dried goji berry and herbal consignment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA audit desks apply automated risk scoring to zero-rated export claims; every refund file is verified against the customs export declaration, carrier data, and IRC. Failure to produce the documentary bundle within the 5-year record retention period triggers retrospective assessment at 14% VAT with monthly late-payment interest (capped at 100% of tax), an administrative penalty of 50% of the tax evaded, and per-invoice fines of EGP 20,000-50,000. Manufactured or forged export documents (fake B/L, circular remittances, inflated quantities) are criminalized under Article 76 of Law No. 67 of 2016: imprisonment of 3 months to 5 years plus a fine of 1-3 times the tax evaded, confiscation of goods, reversal of all input VAT refunds with clawback interest, suspension of the ETA tax card, and blacklisting in the ETA exporter registry, with referral to the Public Funds Prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — General Department of Foreign Exchange
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egyptian Pound (EGP) is partially convertible. Current account transactions, including trade remittances and profit distributions, are generally permitted under CBE Decree No. 40 of 2016 and subsequent liberalization measures. Capital account transactions, such as foreign direct investment injections and shareholder loan repayments, require CBE registration, supporting documentation, and if applicable tax clearance. The 2022–2024 foreign currency rationing created de facto remittance delays; however, the March 2024 exchange rate unification and IMF-supported fiscal program materially improved interbank liquidity and access to hard currency. Profit transfers remain subject to bank verification of audited financial statements, corporate tax payment certificates, and compliance with the CBE's foreign exchange return requirements. Although not a license per se, the company must obtain an authenticated tax card to access bank FX facilities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: As a general rule under CBE instructions applicable to export receipts, 100% of export proceeds from the sale of goods, including dried goji berries and herbal botanicals, must be remitted through a licensed Egyptian bank within 90 days of the date of shipment, and the proceeds must be surrendered to the banking system in EGP at the prevailing interbank exchange rate on the day of receipt. The exporter must present the customs export declaration (SAD/ACI), the commercial invoice, and the filed contract to the negotiating bank. Current CBE guidance allows limited offset for imported production inputs only with prior bank approval. Non-compliance may trigger customs penalties, CBE fines, blacklisting of the exporter, and disqualification from export incentive schemes under the Egyptian Export Development Fund. The company must open a dedicated foreign currency account to temporarily hold incoming wire proceeds before the mandatory conversion date.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.developer_notes: For an EG LLC engaged in ISIC 4631 wholesale of dried herbal botanicals, the CBE's export proceeds surrender regime applies strictly; however, the low-risk nature of the botanical commodity streamlines AML review once full commercial documentation, phytosanitary certifications, and real-party confirmation are supplied.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Foreign Currency Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account, Capital Escrow Account, and Trade Finance Lin
Operational Account and Foreign Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low for principal treasury functions; Medium for ancillary expense management. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business, and Airwallex are not licensed to hold trade-related export proceeds in Egypt and cannot lawfully act as the primary receiving rail for Egyptian customs-cleared exports. CBE Law No. 88 of 1988 and the Payment Councils Law limit payment intermediation to licensed banks and government-approved fintechs. EMIs may be used only for incidental operational expenses outside Egypt, subject to transfer limits and tax disclosure. For the core cross-border receivable cycle, the company must maintain an account at a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank and route all export proceeds through SWIFT MT103 or directly via the bank's correspondent network.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one authorized director, signatory, or legal representative of the EG LLC must appear physically at the Egyptian bank branch for the Corporate KYC Interview and Final Activation Meeting. Remote or video-only onboarding is not accepted for corporate accounts of non-resident legal owners. CBE prudent practice requires the presenting officer to hold a notarized board resolution, valid commercial registration certificate, and a certified memorandum of association. If the managing director cannot travel, a non-resident shareholder may delegate by notarized power of attorney; however, such power must be legalized by the Egyptian consulate or apostille and approved by the bank's compliance committee. Interviews cannot be fully waived for a foreign-owned LLC within the first compliance rating period.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or non-resident shareholder concentration in a high-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the bank with: full corporate ownership chart with individual ultimate beneficial owners above 10%, passport copies, proof of residence, source of wealth statements, bank references from the home jurisdiction, and an in-person explanation of the commercial rationale for the Egyptian entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags, such as price incongruity, unexplained third-party payments, or invoicing mismatches for herbal botanical commodities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a complete trade file including purchase contracts, bills of lading, packing lists, insurance certificates, laboratory certificates of analysis for botanical content, fumigation certificates, customs SAD/ACI declarations, and an independent valuation or benchmark pricing report for dried lycium berries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or politically exposed person screening hits triggered by shareholders, counterparties, or transit ports
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide bank-certified sanctions screening outputs from a recognized database (Dow Jones, World-Check, or Sabre) demonstrating no adverse matches; for any PEP or local intermediary, attach a full source-of-funds file, board approval minutes, and a risk mitigation letter signed by the compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Procedurally safe routing for foreign shareholder capital injection: (1) Obtain General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) approval or attestation for the LLC's capital structure; (2) the investor transfers funds via SWIFT MT103 with proper purpose code 'INVEST' or 'QD' for direct investment, and the beneficiary reference includes the GAFI file number and the LLC's tax card number; (3) the receiving Egyptian bank will register the inward investment on the CBE's investment tracking system and issue an inward remittance certificate; (4) split the funds among the bank's capital escrow account and authorized operational account; (5) after bank verification and inclusion in CBE records, the amount may be used for EGP working capital or liquidated into EGP at the interbank rate without CBE pre-approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound payments related to the dried goji berry trade (e.g., supplier prepayments, freight, insurance, quality inspection fees, and export-related service fees), the company shall instruct SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from its EGP-denominated operational account after conversion to USD/EUR/GBP, with the application describing the trade invoice, contract number, and purpose type 'SUPPLIER PAYMENT UNDER TRADE / COMMERCIAL SERVICES'. Larger disbursements exceeding 20,000 USD should be supported by pro-forma invoice and the parent purchase order. For independent importers, the company may also settle using a commercial letter of credit issued by its Egyptian bank, advising through a confirmed LC at the buyer's bank. The exporter must ensure that all outbound correspondent charges and intermediary bank fees are clearly allocated, to maintain compliance with bank tariff documentation and CBE foreign exchange return filings.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CBE-authorized onshore EGP/USD outright FX forward contracts with a licensed Egyptian bank, tenor normally up to 12 months and requiring a genuine underlying trade exposure
CBE-authorized onshore EGP/EUR outright FX forward contracts with a licensed Egyptian bank for European invoice settlement
Onshore USD/EGP and EUR/EGP FX swap contracts for short-term liquidity mismatches arising from export proceeds timing
Cross-currency swaps for long-term foreign capital liabilities, subject to CBE prior notification and only where the counterparty is a CBE-licensed bank
Non-deliverable forwards on EGP are not permissible for onshore Egyptian legal entities; the company shall not enter such instruments without prior CBE approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months from fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year LLC, by 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers statutory fines and administrative delays (typically EGP 2,000–20,000); repeated default may lead to suspension of tax clearance and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months from fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year LLC, by 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 2% of tax due per month (capped at 100% of tax); willful non-filing may expose managers to criminal sanctions and director disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office (integrated GAFI One-Stop Shop)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March or the registration anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-renewal results in suspension of commercial activity, fines up to EGP 5,000, and potential deregistration of the LLC from the Commercial Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Annual Confirmation and Shareholding Disclosure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the triggering event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file subjects the LLC to fines up to EGP 10,000 and criminal liability for intentional concealment of UBO information.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all Egyptian LLCs irrespective of revenue, assets, or headcount (Companies Law No. 159/1981, Art. 42; Investment Law No. 72/2017).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), aligned with IFRS; consolidated holdings and listed entities must apply full IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: File an annual UBO declaration with GAFI confirming the register of members, any share transfers, and the natural person(s) owning or controlling 25% or more. Changes in beneficial ownership must be notarized and registered within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Commercial Registry Certificate and Trade License

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% (flat corporate income tax for commercial and industrial companies, Law No. 91 of 2005 as amended by Law No. 2 of 2023)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday for a standard LLC. Available preferences: Law No. 1 of 2023 allows up to a 50% tax credit for strategic projects approved by the Supreme Council for Investment; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 permits deduction of 30-50% of investment costs in priority geographic zones; licensed free-zone entities inside the Suez Canal Economic Zone may benefit from a 0% rate on export profits; dividends received from Egyptian affiliates are exempt from CIT for resident corporate shareholders.
